na.action: encourage the drawing up of codes of conduct

na.subject: PD-022
na.action: prepare, amend or extend codes of conduct specifying the application of the Regulation (matters (a)-(k))

na.subject: controllers or processors not subject to the Regulation (Art.3)
na.action: adhere to approved codes of conduct with general validity to provide appropriate safeguards for transfers
na.conditions: code approved under 40(5) and with general validity under 40(9); binding and enforceable commitments

na.subject: code of conduct (content requirement; addressee: association preparing it)
na.action: contain mechanisms enabling the body referred to in Art.41(1) to carry out mandatory monitoring of compliance

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: register and publish an approved code, amendment or extension

na.subject: European Commission

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: ensure appropriate publicity for approved codes with general validity

na.subject: PD-015

na.subject: Member States, supervisory authorities, the Board and the Commission

na.subject: approved certification mechanisms, seals or marks (and controllers/processors not subject to the Regulation)

na.conditions: approved under 42(5); transfers under Art.46(2)(f)

na.subject: (certification — subject not named)

na.subject: certification (effect clause)
na.action: does not reduce the responsibility of the controller or processor; without prejudice to the tasks and powers of competent supervisory authorities

na.subject: PD-015

na.object: register of certification mechanisms and seals

na.subject: Member States

na.note: Obligation on Member States; instances of accreditors are not created by the Regulation.

na.subject: PD-024
na.action: be responsible for the proper assessment leading to certification or withdrawal, without prejudice to the controller's/processor's responsibility; accreditation for a maximum of five years, renewable

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: make requirements and criteria public in an easily accessible form (corrigendum: sentence on the Board register removed)

na.subject: European Commission

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: adopt implementing acts laying down technical standards for certification mechanisms and seals and marks, and mechanisms to promote and recognise them
na.conditions: examination procedure of Art.93(2)

na.subject: controller and processor
na.action: transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation only if the Chapter V conditions are complied with, including for onward transfers

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: decide that a third country, territory, sector or international organisation ensures an adequate level of protection (enabling transfers without specific authorisation)
na.conditions: Commission decision; transfer then requires no specific authorisation
na.note: The adequacy decision is an act of the Commission, not an institutional device; INS-TYPE.

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: take account of listed elements (rule of law, independent supervisory authorities in the third country, international commitments) when assessing adequacy
na.note: Point (b) refers to independent supervisory authorities of the third country and cooperation with Member States' SAs (position outside W).

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: adopt an adequacy decision by implementing act with a periodic review mechanism (at least every four years), specifying territorial/sectoral application and identifying the third-country supervisory authority
na.conditions: examination procedure of Art.93(2); after assessment

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: monitor on an ongoing basis developments in third countries and international organisations that could affect adequacy decisions (including decisions under Art.25(6) of Directive 95/46/EC)

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: repeal, amend or suspend an adequacy decision where information reveals that adequacy is no longer ensured; immediately applicable implementing acts on imperative grounds of urgency (Art.93(3))
na.conditions: available information, esp. following the review; examination procedure Art.93(2); urgency: Art.93(3)

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: publish in the Official Journal and on its website the list of countries, territories, sectors and international organisations for which adequacy is or is no longer ensured

na.subject: controller and processor
na.action: transfer personal data to a third country only if appropriate safeguards have been provided and enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies are available
na.conditions: absence of an adequacy decision under 45(3)

na.subject: controller and processor
na.action: provide appropriate safeguards without specific SA authorisation by: (a) instrument between public authorities; (b) binding corporate rules (Art.47); (c) standard data protection clauses adopted by the Commission (Art.93(2)); (d) standard clauses adopted by a SA and approved by the Commission (Art.93(2)); (e) approved code of conduct (Art.40) with commitments; (f) approved certification mechanism (Art.42) with commitments
na.conditions: no specific authorisation from a supervisory authority required
na.depends_on: binding corporate rules (Art.47); standard data protection clauses; approved code of conduct (Art.40); approved certification mechanism (Art.42)

na.action: apply the consistency mechanism (Art.63) in the cases referred to in 46(3)

na.note: Contains internal oversight and reporting relations (j),(k),(l),(m) toward the competent SA — recorded as content requirements; no relation is asserted among actual group members.

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: specify the format and procedures for the exchange of information between controllers, processors and supervisory authorities for BCR
na.object: format and procedures for BCR information exchange
na.conditions: examination procedure of Art.93(2)

na.subject: controller
na.action: transfer data in the absence of adequacy or appropriate safeguards only on conditions (a)-(g) or, as a last resort, where the transfer is not repetitive, concerns a limited number of data subjects, is necessary for compelling legitimate interests and suitable safeguards are provided after the controller's assessment
na.conditions: absence of Art.45(3) decision and of Art.46 safeguards; conditions (a)-(g)
na.note: Conditions of lawfulness; point (g) refers to registers 'which according to Union or Member State law' are intended to provide information to the public (registers not constituted here).

na.subject: Union or Member State law (legislator not named)
na.action: expressly set limits to the transfer of specific categories of personal data to a third country or international organisation, for important reasons of public interest
na.conditions: absence of an adequacy decision

na.subject: controller and processor
na.action: document the assessment and the suitable safeguards in the records referred to in Art.30

na.subject: Member States
na.action: provide for one or more independent public authorities responsible for monitoring the application of the Regulation ('supervisory authority')

na.subject: supervisory authority

na.subject: (dismissing authority — not stated)

na.action: provide by law for: (a) the establishment of each supervisory authority; (b)-(f) qualifications, appointment rules and procedures, term of office (no less than four years), reappointment, obligations and incompatibilities of members and staff
na.object: establishment and organisation of supervisory authorities
na.norm_type: N2 (obligation to provide by law for establishment)
na.note: Confirms that the supervisory authorities are constituted by Member State law (outside W); the GDPR obliges Member States to do so.

na.action: be subject to a duty of professional secrecy during and after the term of office, including regarding reporting by natural persons of infringements
na.conditions: in accordance with Union or Member State law

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: be competent for the tasks assigned and powers conferred by the Regulation on the territory of its own Member State

na.conditions: processing by public authorities or private bodies acting under Art.6(1)(c),(e)
na.note: Excludes the lead-authority mechanism.

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: not be competent to supervise processing operations of courts acting in their judicial capacity

na.subject: supervisory authority

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: on its territory perform the tasks (a)-(v), without prejudice to other tasks under the Regulation

na.conditions: on its territory

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: (b) promote public awareness; (d) promote controllers'/processors' awareness; (i) monitor relevant developments; (u) keep internal records of infringements and measures under Art.58(2); (v) fulfil any other tasks
na.object: awareness, monitoring of developments, internal records, residual tasks

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: perform tasks free of charge for the data subject and, where applicable, the DPO

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: authorise processing referred to in Art.36(5) if the law of the Member State requires prior authorisation
na.conditions: Member State law requires prior authorisation
na.note: Authorization power exists only if national law requires it; relation to controllers arises under that law.

na.subject: (Union and Member State law)
na.action: subject the exercise of the SA's powers to appropriate safeguards, including effective judicial remedy and due process, in accordance with the Charter
na.note: Links SA powers to judicial review (Art.78).

na.subject: Member States
na.action: provide by law that the supervisory authority has the power to bring infringements to the attention of judicial authorities and, where appropriate, to commence or engage in legal proceedings to enforce the Regulation
na.norm_type: N2-like (obligation to confer a power by national law)

na.subject: Member States
na.action: may provide by law that the SA has additional powers; their exercise shall not impair the effective operation of Chapter VII

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: specify by implementing acts the format and procedures for mutual assistance and the electronic exchange of information between SAs and between SAs and the Board
na.object: format and procedures for mutual assistance
na.conditions: examination procedure of Art.93(2)

na.subject: supervisory authoritys (and, where relevant, the Commission)
na.action: cooperate with each other, and where relevant with the Commission, through the consistency mechanism as set out in Section 2, to contribute to consistent application
na.note: Names the mechanism and refers to Section 2 for its rules; the mechanism is set out, not 'established'.

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: issue an opinion on matters submitted under 64(1),(2) within eight weeks by simple majority (extendable by six weeks), provided no opinion on the same matter has been issued; a member not objecting within a reasonable period is deemed to agree
na.conditions: matter submitted; opinion not already issued

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: adopt its decision within two weeks after the second month by simple majority; the Chair's vote decides if split
na.conditions: Board unable to decide within the 65(2) periods

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: adopt an urgent opinion or urgent binding decision within two weeks by simple majority (derogation from Arts 64(3) and 65(2))
na.conditions: requests under 66(2),(3)

na.subject: European Commission
na.action: adopt implementing acts of general scope specifying the arrangements for the exchange of information by electronic means between SAs and between SAs and the Board, in particular the standardised format in Art.64
na.conditions: examination procedure of Art.93(2)

na.subject: (Union legislator, by the provision itself)
na.action: establish the European Data Protection Board as a body of the Union with legal personality
na.note: N1: the Regulation itself establishes the Board. Legal status per Art.99: applicable from 25 May 2018. Material establishment/operation not assessed.

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: be represented by its Chair

na.subject: Member States with more than one supervisory authority
na.action: appoint a joint representative in accordance with Member State law

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: act independently when performing its tasks or exercising its powers under Arts 70 and 71

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: neither seek nor take instructions from anybody in performing its tasks (without prejudice to Commission requests under Art.70(1),(2))
na.conditions: corrigendum 2018: 'Article 70(1) and (2)'
na.note: Commission requests under Art.70(1),(2) are excepted (no instruction).

na.subject: European Data Protection Board

na.note: 25 points inventoried; relation-bearing points extracted below; points already extracted elsewhere are linked.

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: maintain a public register of certification mechanisms and data protection seals and marks (Art.42(8)) and of certified controllers/processors established in third countries (Art.42(7)) (o); maintain a publicly accessible electronic register of decisions of supervisory authorities and courts on issues handled in the consistency mechanism (y)
na.depends_on: register of certification mechanisms and seals; register of consistency-mechanism decisions

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: take decisions by a simple majority of its members unless otherwise provided

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: adopt its own rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority and organise its own operational arrangements

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: elect a chair and two deputy chairs from among its members by simple majority

na.subject: Chair of the Board
na.action: convene meetings and prepare the agenda; notify Art.65 decisions to the lead SA and SAs concerned; ensure timely performance of the Board's tasks, in particular in relation to the consistency mechanism

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: lay down the allocation of tasks between the Chair and the deputy chairs in its rules of procedure

na.subject: European Data Protection Board
na.action: keep its discussions confidential where it deems it necessary, as provided in its rules of procedure

na.subject: proceedings against a supervisory authority (parties)
na.action: be brought before the courts of the Member State where the supervisory authority is established
na.object: forum for review of SA decisions

na.subject: proceedings against a controller or processor (parties)
na.action: be brought before the courts of the Member State where the controller/processor has an establishment, or alternatively where the data subject habitually resides (unless a public authority acting in its public powers)

na.subject: controller / processor
na.action: be exempt from liability if it proves it is not in any way responsible for the event giving rise to the damage
na.conditions: proof of non-responsibility

na.subject: court proceedings for compensation (parties)
na.action: be brought before the courts competent under the law of the Member State referred to in Art.79(2)

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: ensure that administrative fines are in each individual case effective, proportionate and dissuasive

na.subject: supervisory authority

na.conditions: intentional or negligent infringement of several provisions for the same or linked processing operations

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: impose administrative fines up to EUR 20 000 000 or 4 % of worldwide annual turnover for infringements of: (a) Arts 5, 6, 7, 9; (b) Arts 12–22; (c) Arts 44–49; (d) obligations under Member State law adopted under Chapter IX; (e) non-compliance with a limitation/suspension order or failure to provide access in violation of Art.58(1)

na.subject: Member States
na.action: may lay down rules on whether and to what extent administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies established in the Member State
na.conditions: without prejudice to Art.58(2) corrective powers

na.subject: supervisory authority
na.action: exercise its powers under Art.83 subject to appropriate procedural safeguards in accordance with Union and Member State law, including effective judicial remedy and due process

na.action: lay down the rules on other penalties for infringements not subject to administrative fines and take all measures to ensure that they are implemented; penalties effective, proportionate and dissuasive

na.subject: Member States
na.action: reconcile by law the right to protection of personal data with freedom of expression and information, including journalistic, academic, artistic or literary expression

na.subject: rules adopted under 88(1) (content requirement)

na.subject: controllers (processing for archiving, research or statistical purposes)

na.subject: Union or Member State law (legislator not named)
na.action: provide for derogations from Arts 15, 16, 18, 21 for scientific/historical research or statistical purposes, subject to the safeguards in 89(1)

na.subject: Union or Member State law (legislator not named)
na.action: provide for derogations from Arts 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21 for archiving purposes in the public interest, subject to the safeguards in 89(1)

na.subject: Member States
na.action: adopt specific rules setting out the powers of supervisory authorities under Art.58(1)(e),(f) in relation to controllers/processors subject to professional secrecy, where necessary and proportionate

na.subject: churches and religious associations or communities (Member State)

na.subject: European Commission

na.action: if necessary submit appropriate proposals to amend the Regulation, taking into account developments in information technology and the information society

na.action: if appropriate submit legislative proposals to amend other Union legal acts on the protection of personal data, in particular for processing by Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
na.conditions: if appropriate

Long lists (Art.4 definitions; Art.57(1) 22 tasks; Art.58 powers; Art.70(1) 25 tasks; Art.83(4)-(5) tiers) were grouped into few records, with point citations only where relation-bearing points were separated or linked.

unc.description: Possible duplicate observations: the complaint-handling duty of the SA appears in QR for Art.57(1)(f) (with Art.77 units linked), Art.77(2) and Art.60(7). They were kept as distinct statements by unit but state overlapping duties.
unc.effect: Counts of relations in SC-10 and SC-07 may overstate independent observations; many-to-many provenance (not duplication) is the intended rule.

unc.description: Relation type 'information/reporting' is used for 106 of 238 relations (44.5%) and lumps notifications, consultations, cooperation, reasons-giving and information duties. V6's ten relation types do not provide a type for peer cooperation, jurisdictional or liability allocation.
unc.effect: Type-level analyses (e.g. 'information relations dominate') are artefacts of the type inventory; discrimination is carried by `function`, `object` and `type_note`.

unc.effect: AC (full) appears only as a derived, cross-provision relation; no single unit satisfies all five elements.

unc.description: Twenty assignments have an unstated or unnamed subject ('Union or Member State law', passive voice, unspecified legislator). They are recorded as NA with `subject-unstated`; no actor was invented.

hq.issue: Do procedures (cooperation under Art.60, mutual assistance, joint operations, the consistency mechanism, the urgency procedure) meet the DEV threshold (identity + operator/rules/bounded function), and are they devices at all?
hq.why_it_matters: Ten PD records are flagged DEV-threshold. Treating procedures as devices inflates the device category; treating them as relations loses their identity as a legally set-out procedure with its own rules.
hq.options: (a) procedures as DEV; (b) procedures as sets of relations (INS-TYPE); (c) a separate 'procedure' kind

hq.issue: Is an 'obligation to designate/appoint an office-holder' (DPO, representative, joint representative) an N2 or a separate norm type?
hq.why_it_matters: The Regulation specifies the office at type level; the instance arises from a private act. N1–N4 do not state who constitutes the instance.
hq.options: (a) N2-designation as used here; (b) new norm type; (c) record only the duty

hq.issue: Does the 'mediated constitution' of the national supervisory authorities (Union obligation in Arts 51(1)/54(1)(a) → establishment by Member State law) count as 'legally constituted' within W?
hq.why_it_matters: The formal architecture of the GDPR contains the obligation and the competence, not the authorities. V6's 'legally constituted configuration' must say by which legal order.
hq.options: (a) only the obligation is constituted within W; (b) a two-step category of mediated constitution; (c) widen W to national law

hq.issue: From what date does the N1 establishment of the Board (Art.68(1)) take effect — entry into force (24 May 2016) or application (25 May 2018)?
hq.why_it_matters: Determines the temporal reference of the 'legal constitution evidenced' claim for the Board; Art.92(2) shows provisions with effect from entry into force.
hq.options: (a) 25 May 2018; (b) 24 May 2016; (c) not determinable from W

hq.issue: Is a derived controller/processor→SA relation satisfying all five accountability elements across several provisions (5(2), 24(1), 58(1)(a),(e), 58(2), 83) admissible as ACCOUNTABILITY under DR-10?
hq.why_it_matters: It is the only candidate for full AC in W; the 'questioning' capacity rests on 58(1)(a),(e). The classification depends on how strictly derivation across provisions is allowed.
hq.options: (a) admit as derived; (b) require a single provision; (c) require explicit questioning capacity

hq.issue: Should 'questioning capacity' be required explicitly? (Board→SA after 64(8); courts→SA; legislature→Commission).
hq.why_it_matters: Without it the relations stay ANSWERABILITY or INFO although assessment and consequences exist. The requirement may be too strict for institutions whose procedures are set outside W.
hq.options: (a) keep as is; (b) accept institutionally implied questioning where a binding review decision exists

hq.issue: Do V6's ten relation types suffice? Peer cooperation, liability allocation, jurisdiction rules and court-to-court coordination had no type; 106 of 238 relations are 'information/reporting'.
hq.why_it_matters: Type inflation hides differences relevant to S→A (consultation, escalation, standstill).
hq.options: (a) keep and rely on `function` and `type_note`; (b) add secondary subtypes; (c) propose an additional type to David

hq.issue: Independent re-discovery of subconfigurations: the S predicates were written by the same agent after extraction.
hq.why_it_matters: Candidate S may encode the analyst's expectations; false positives were found in SC-10.
hq.options: A second coder defines S blind to these; compare; or use a documented clustering method as a comparator

hq.issue: Competing S→A hypotheses with consequential outcomes: AI-03 (conditional integration), AI-04 (shared interfaces vs one assurance architecture), AI-05 (indeterminate), AI-07 (mediated constitution), AI-08 (W=A not supported).
hq.why_it_matters: These are the pilot's substantive claims.
hq.options: Independent legal review and blind recoding of coupling (I2) for each AI record

hq.issue: Retrieve and read Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 (committee procedure) and the instrument constituting the EDPS before any claim on Commission rule-making control (AI-05) or on the Board's membership.
hq.why_it_matters: Decisive external dependencies for AI-05 and AI-07.
hq.options: Targeted retrieval of the cited Articles only (no automatic corpus expansion)

hq.issue: Art.62(7): referent of 'its Member State' ('may adopt a provisional measure on the territory of its Member State').
hq.options: Specialist legal reading; recital and case-law check

hq.issue: Is 'Union or Member State law' (an unnamed legislator) a position, an origin of competence, or neither?
hq.why_it_matters: 20 NA records have unstated subjects; the architecture of rule-making competence is partly represented through them.
hq.options: Treat as source of norms (not a position); record competence only

hq.issue: Does optionality of enhancement (codes 'may'; certification 'voluntary') defeat the V6 'institutionalized enhancement' condition for enhanced self-regulation (AI-09)?
hq.why_it_matters: Determines whether the pattern is a property of the instrument or only of adherents.
hq.options: (a) conditional layer (as recorded); (b) condition not met

hq.issue: Later amendments to the GDPR and later official corrigenda after 3 October 2026 were not verified.
